title: Draft: Qt: Use deleteLater() to delete context menus.
description:
A recent change set the WA_DeleteOnClose attribute on many of our
context menus. It looks like this can cause crashes in some situations,
for example when we try to use sender() in the code triggered by the
menu as suggested by the stack traces in #18282 and #18315.

Connect the menu's triggered signal to deleteLater instead of setting
WA_DeleteOnClose. This should avoid any race conditions we might run
into when trying to access context menus or their actions after they've
been triggered. Delete our context menus in a couple of places where we
weren't doing so.

Fixes #18251 and related bugs.

notes.body:
Should these be flagged with comments, so that somebody doesn't look at the code and say "why not mark these as delete-on-close?"

Does this mean that the menu stays visible until the action requested from the menu completes?  Or is the menu hidden as soon as you select the item but not *deleted*, in the "free it" sense, until later?)

(And is there another way for the function connected to the signal to get the information it needs to perform the action?  Does this problem not occur with, for example, menu items from the menu bar, because those menus don't get deleted after you've selected an item from them?)

> Should these be flagged with comments, so that somebody doesn't look at the code and say "why not mark these as delete-on-close?"

I think so, whatever our fix might be. After pushing this I realized that the `triggered` signal probably won't fire if the user doesn't select anything (e.g. if they hit the Escape key or click outside the menu), which will leak memory. A better solution might be to make each context menu a persistent member variable and `clear()` it before filling it in. @rknall & @desowin what do you think?

> Does this mean that the menu stays visible until the action requested from the menu completes? Or is the menu hidden as soon as you select the item but not *deleted*, in the "free it" sense, until later?)

If I read [qmenu.cpp](https://github.com/qt/qtbase/blob/6.2.4/src/widgets/widgets/qmenu.cpp) correctly, it's the latter. Closing / hiding the menu is a result of mouse or keyboard interaction. Deletion happens separately and is our responsibility.

> (And is there another way for the function connected to the signal to get the information it needs to perform the action? 

Possibly. In the case of the "Copy as" issues (#18282 and #18315), the data to copy is attached to a QActionGroup via the "idataprintable" property. It looks like that gets deleted before DataPrinter::copyIDataBytes can access it. We could probably find another path to deliver the data, but I think it would be easier and less complex to just make the menu persistent. 

> Does this problem not occur with, for example, menu items from the menu bar, because those menus don't get deleted after you've selected an item from them?)

That's correct.

With this patch applied and tested on macOS I'm no longer seeing the following console message in Terminal window upon exiting Wireshark after opening and closing the Follow TCP dialogs from context menu:

```
 ** (wireshark:19680) 09:43:58.835663 [GUI WARNING] -- QObject: shared QObject was deleted directly. The program is malformed and may crash.
```

Without this patch if the Follow dialog was opened from context menu and Wireshark had not crashed before choosing to exit the message above was reliably reported upon exit.

With this patch applied and tested on Windows 10 system I'm no longer seeing Wireshark spontaneously exit after closing an open pcap file after having opened and closed a Follow TCP dialog from the context menu.

This is confusing. The Qt::WA_DeleteOnClose attribute calls `deleteLater()`:

https://github.com/qt/qtbase/blob/5.15.2/src/widgets/kernel/qwidget.cpp#L8276

The problem is related to nested event loops, just like !8038. `FollowStreamDialog::readFollowStream()` calls `mainApp->processEvents();` and thus the pending `deleteLater()` is processed prematurely. Remove the `mainApp->processEvents();` call and the crash will come later when opening menu (same reason, i.e. `processEvents()` called in another code path). Remove all `processEvents()` calls and the problem is gone (but so is the progress notification and UI freezes until the processing is done).

The long term solution is to get rid of all `exec()` and `processEvents()` calls, but doing so is not simple.

The reason why this MR works is that this MR causes `deleteLater()` to be executed *after* `WiresharkMainWindow::on_actionAnalyzeFollowTCPStream_triggered()`. The culprit is `processEvents()` processes the pending delete while the QMenu handling has not finished. When the processing returns back to `QAction::activate()` it returns into `QMenuPrivate::activateCausedStack()` but the object has been already deleted and hence the crash.

For the time being just connecting the actions with `Qt::QueuedConnection` instead of `Qt::AutoConnection` is probably the best solution.
Thanks for looking into this. Closing this in favor of !8088 and !8097.
